# SI units and prefixes — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/si-units.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/si-units.ttl`](../decks/si-units.ttl) · **Cards:** 53 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

The International System of Units (SI) in 53 cards: the 7 base units, the 22 derived units with special names and the 24 SI prefixes, including ronna, quetta, ronto and quecto from 2022. The front names a quantity or a prefix; the back gives the SI unit with its symbol, or the prefix's factor and symbol. Compiled from NIST's SI guide and prefix table, Swedac's regulations on units of measurement (STAFS 2009:26) and Wikidata, and checked against the BIPM SI Brochure.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0 1.0. Its content sources are all public domain or CC0. NIST SP 811 is a work of NIST employees, not subject to copyright in the United States; elsewhere NIST grants a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free right to reprint it and make derivative works. NIST's prefix page is, under NIST's website terms, public information that may be distributed or copied (it is not marked as copyrighted). In any case the deck takes only facts from NIST (unit and prefix names, symbols, factors, the year the four newest prefixes were added), which are not copyrightable. STAFS 2009:26 is a Swedish statute, which Swedish copyright law (9 § upphovsrättslagen) excludes from copyright; Wikidata is CC0. The card wording is our own. The BIPM SI Brochure (CC BY 4.0) and Swedish Wikipedia's prefix table (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used only to verify facts the content sources gave (names, symbols, factors, the unit-one convention for angles, the 2022 adoption); no text and no selection was taken from them — the selection, the complete set of named SI units and prefixes, comes from NIST. NIST SP 330, the US edition of the BIPM brochure, was deliberately not used because it carries a BIPM copyright notice. The sources are nevertheless credited in the deck and in this report.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. Units in English: downloaded NIST SP 811 (2008) as PDF and extracted its text with pypdf. Table 1 (SI base units, PDF p. 16) gave the 7 base units and Table 3 ("The 22 SI coherent derived units with special names and symbols", PDF p. 17) the 22 derived units: for each, the quantity, the unit name and the symbol. Where a row names several quantities ("energy, work, amount of heat") the card names the first one, which is unique among the 29 units.
3. Prefixes: downloaded NIST's Metric (SI) Prefixes page and read its table of 24 prefixes (name, symbol, factor 10^30 to 10^−30). The deck uses all 24.
4. Swedish: downloaded the consolidated Swedac regulation STAFS 2009:26 om måttenheter (amended up to STAFS 2020:2) and extracted its text. Bilaga 1.1 (SI-grundenheter), 1.1.1 (Celsiustemperatur), 1.2.3 (Härledda SI-enheter med särskilda namn och beteckningar) and 1.3 (Multipelprefix) gave the Swedish quantity names, unit names and the 20 prefixes it lists (hekto, deka, mikro, piko, yokto ...). Where STAFS names several quantities for one unit the card uses the one that matches the English front ("elektrisk laddning", "elektrisk spänning").
5. The four prefixes adopted in 2022 (ronna, quetta, ronto, quecto) are not in STAFS 2009:26. Their Swedish names were taken from the Swedish labels of their Wikidata items (ronna, quetta, ronto, quekto) and checked against the prefix table of Swedish Wikipedia (Mall:SI-prefix: Quetta, Ronna, Ronto, Quekto).
6. Wikidata: SPARQL queries (see Queries) fetched, for the 29 units, their English and Swedish labels and aliases, unit symbols (P5061) and measured quantities (P111) with the quantities' labels; and for every item that is an instance of SI prefix (Q131299), its labels, symbol (P5061) and numeric value (P1181). English unit names follow the international (BIPM and Wikidata) spelling: metre, deca; NIST's US spellings meter and deka are given in a note.
7. Card text: fronts read "SI unit of <quantity>" / "SI-enhet för <storhet>" for units and the bare prefix name with the note "SI prefix" for prefixes. Backs give the unit name and symbol, "newton (N)", in English and Swedish, or the factor and symbol of a prefix, "10³ (k)", untagged since it has no language. The micro sign is the Greek letter μ (U+03BC), as on NIST's page and in Wikidata. Unit names are lower case, as the SI requires; "Celsius" keeps its capital. Notes say whether a unit is a base unit or a derived unit with a special name, and point out the pairs that share a dimension (Hz and Bq, Gy and Sv). Further notes: the radian and steradian notes follow the current BIPM brochure (Section 2.3.3: plane and solid angle are treated as quantities with the unit one by convention), backed by NIST SP 811 Table 3 (expressed as 1), after QC round 1 found SP 811's 2008 wording out of date; the degree Celsius note (equal to the kelvin, t/°C = T/K − 273.15) comes from NIST SP 811 Section 4.2.1.1 and STAFS bilaga 1.1.1; kilo's lower-case symbol from NIST's prefix page (Capitalization), checked against BIPM Section 3.1; the year 2022 and the four prefixes added together from NIST's prefix page (Prefix Progress table), checked against Wikidata P571 and BIPM Resolution 3 of the 27th CGPM; the alternative Swedish names of illuminance (belysningsstyrka, illuminans) from Wikidata Q194411; the US spellings meter and deka from NIST.
8. Cross-check: every card was compared against the BIPM SI Brochure (9th edition, V4.01, June 2026; Table 2 base units, Table 4 the 22 derived units, Table 7 the 24 prefixes, and Resolution 3 of the 27th CGPM for the 2022 prefixes) and against Wikidata through the builder's machine checks: the English and Swedish label of each unit and prefix, its symbol, each prefix's numeric value and SI-prefix class, each unit's measured quantity, and the English and Swedish labels of the quantities wherever Wikidata uses the card's wording. Where Wikidata disagreed with the official sources the check was left out and the discrepancy recorded (Quality control, round 0).
9. Not used: NIST SP 330 (2019), the US edition of the SI Brochure, was downloaded (see Queries) and read for its licence only: it carries the BIPM's note that "All BIPM's works are internationally protected by copyright", so it is not a public-domain source, and it predates the 2022 prefixes.
10. Swedish forms of the 2022 prefixes: no Swedish regulation or authority lists them yet (STAFS 2009:26 stops at yotta and yokto), so 'ronna', 'quetta', 'ronto' and 'quekto' rest on Wikidata's Swedish labels and Swedish Wikipedia only. The quekto card says so in its Swedish note. The web search behind this claim was not logged at authoring; in QC round 4 it was re-run on 2026-10-04 (two web searches, terms under Queries). Neither found guidance from Swedac, RISE or Språkrådet on Swedish forms of the 2022 prefixes. The second listed STAFS 2022:6, which was downloaded and checked: it amends STAFS 2016:1 on measuring instruments, not STAFS 2009:26, and the consolidated STAFS 2009:26 still ends at the amendment STAFS 2020:2.
11. Text extraction: PDFs with pypdf and the NIST HTML pages with Beautiful Soup (see Queries). The original extraction commands were not logged in full during authoring; in QC round 3 the commands listed under Queries were re-run on 2026-10-04 and produce the text files used for the cards byte for byte, and the re-downloaded NIST SP 330 PDF has the same SHA-256 as the copy read at authoring.

## Selection

All of the core SI: the 7 base units, the 22 derived units with special names and symbols (as listed in NIST SP 811 Table 3 and BIPM SI Brochure Table 4, including the radian, steradian, degree Celsius and katal), and the 24 SI prefixes from quetta (10³⁰) to quecto (10⁻³⁰) as listed by NIST. Left out: derived units without special names (square metre, metre per second ...), non-SI units accepted for use with the SI (litre, tonne, minute, electronvolt ...), the binary prefixes (kibi, mebi ...), which are IEC, not SI, and the defining constants. One card per unit and per prefix; for units with several quantities the first quantity named in the tables is on the front.

**sparql.py, the helper that ran every SPARQL query below: python3 sparql.py <query file> <out.csv>** (Wikidata)

```
import sys, urllib.request, urllib.parse
q = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
data = urllib.parse.urlencode({"query": q}).encode()
req = urllib.request.Request("https://query.wikidata.org/sparql", data=data, headers={
    "User-Agent": "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)",
    "Accept": "text/csv"})
out = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120).read().decode()
open(sys.argv[2], "w").write(out)
print(out)
```

**First attempt: instances of SI base unit (Q223662), SI derived unit (Q208469) and Q181508 (mistakenly guessed to be the SI prefix class; it is not). Too broad: it returned thousands of prefixed units and unrelated items, and was discarded. Run with: python3 sparql.py <query file> <out.csv> (the helper is listed under Queries).** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?item ?class ?en ?sv (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?sym; separator=" | ") AS ?syms) WHERE {
  VALUES ?class { wd:Q223662 wd:Q208469 wd:Q181508 }
  ?item wdt:P31 ?class .
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P5061 ?sym }
} GROUP BY ?item ?class ?en ?sv ORDER BY ?class ?en
```

**The 29 units by English label (timed out with HTTP 504; replaced by the next query)** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?name ?item ?sv (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT CONCAT(STR(?sym), "@", LANG(?sym)); separator=" | ") AS ?syms) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STR(?cls); separator=" ") AS ?classes) WHERE {
  VALUES ?name { "metre" "kilogram" "second" "ampere" "kelvin" "mole" "candela"
    "radian" "steradian" "hertz" "newton" "pascal" "joule" "watt" "coulomb" "volt" "farad" "ohm"
    "siemens" "weber" "tesla" "henry" "degree Celsius" "lumen" "lux" "becquerel" "gray" "sievert" "katal" }
  ?item rdfs:label ?l .
  FILTER(STR(?l) = ?name && LANG(?l) = "en")
  ?item wdt:P5061 ?sym .
  ?item wdt:P31 ?cls .
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
} GROUP BY ?name ?item ?sv ORDER BY ?name
```

**Every instance of SI prefix (Q131299): labels, Swedish aliases, symbol, numeric value** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?item ?en ?sv (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?sym; separator=" | ") AS ?syms) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT STR(?num); separator=" | ") AS ?nums) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT CONCAT(STR(?svAlt)); separator=" | ") AS ?svAlts) WHERE {
  ?item wdt:P31 wd:Q131299 .
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }

} GROUP BY ?item ?en ?sv ORDER BY ?en
```

```
  OPTIONAL { ?unit rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?unit skos:altLabel ?alt FILTER(LANG(?alt) = "sv") }
} GROUP BY ?unit ?en ?sv ORDER BY ?en
```

## Quality control

7 rounds, 39 findings: 22 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 17 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (285 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Source agreement and machine checks: every card against NIST (SP 811, prefix page), Swedac STAFS 2009:26, the BIPM SI Brochure and Wikidata. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 53 cards; the licences of all sources.

276 Wikidata checks pass (python3 scripts/authored_decks.py check si-units, 2026-10-04): for every unit its English label, Swedish label (except two, below), symbol (P5061) and, for 27 units, measured quantity (P111); for every prefix its English and Swedish label, symbol, numeric value (P1181) and class SI prefix (Q131299); and the English or Swedish label of the quantity on the front wherever Wikidata uses the card's wording. All 29 units and 24 prefixes agree in name, symbol and factor across NIST, the BIPM brochure and Wikidata; the Swedish unit and prefix names agree between STAFS 2009:26 and Wikidata except where noted. Discrepancies and how they were resolved are listed as findings; no check was dropped to make the build pass other than those listed.

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 53 cards, against the BIPM SI Brochure (V4.01, June 2026), NIST's prefix page and STAFS 2009:26; the builder's Wikidata checks re-run.

No factual errors in fronts or backs. The radian and steradian notes used NIST SP 811's 2008 wording ("a special name for the number one"), which the current BIPM brochure no longer uses; both notes now follow BIPM Section 2.3.3. The Swedish 'quekto' has no official Swedish source; the card now says so. Two optional notes (Celsius, lux) were added. All findings verified against the scratch copies of the sources and applied.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| radian | The note 'a special name for the number one' comes only from NIST SP 811 (2008), note (b); the current BIPM brochure says the representation rad = m/m 'is not intrinsic and may be misleading' and that angles are treated as quantities with the unit one 'for reasons of history and convention' (Section 2.3.3). | Verified in the BIPM text (Section 2.3.3, PDF p. 22; Table 4 footnote (b), PDF p. 24). Note changed to "One of the 22 SI derived units with special names. By convention the SI treats plane angle as a quantity with the unit one." / "… Inom SI behandlas plan vinkel av konvention som en storhet med enheten ett." Evidence: SP 811 Table 3 (expressed as 1) with BIPM Section 2.3.3 and footnote (b). | fixed |
| steradian | Same out-of-date 'number one' note as the radian; BIPM Table 4 footnote (c) says sr = m²/m² 'is not intrinsic and may be misleading'. | Verified (BIPM Table 4 footnote (c), PDF p. 24). Note changed in the same way, for solid angle / rymdvinkel; evidence as for the radian. | fixed |
| prefix-quecto | The Swedish 'quekto' rests only on Wikidata and sv.wikipedia; STAFS 2009:26 (to 2020:2) predates 2022 and no Swedish authority confirms the spelling. | Confirmed: STAFS's prefix table stops at yotta and yokto. Kept 'quekto' and added to the Swedish note: "Stavningen quekto följer mönstret yokto och piko; Swedacs föreskrifter tar ännu inte upp prefixet. Internationellt: quecto." STAFS bilaga 1.3 added as evidence; the lack of an official Swedish source was already in round 0 and is now also a method step. | fixed |
| degree-celsius | The front contains 'Celsius', so it gives most of the answer away; suggested a note that teaches something. | Added the note "Equal in size to the kelvin: t/°C = T/K − 273.15." / "Lika stor som kelvin: t/°C = T/K − 273,15." with evidence from NIST SP 811 (Section 4.2.1.1, Appendix B.8), STAFS bilaga 1.1.1 and BIPM Section 2.3.1. The front keeps the official quantity name (Celsius temperature / Celsiustemperatur), which is the only correct name. | fixed |
| lux | Swedish 'belysning' follows STAFS but reads as 'lighting'; learners know 'belysningsstyrka'. | Added to the Swedish note: "Storheten kallas även belysningsstyrka eller illuminans." Wikidata Q194411 has the label 'illuminans' and the aliases 'belysningsstyrka' and 'belysning'; three label checks added. | fixed |
| deck | NIST SP 811 (2008) predates the 2019 redefinition and the 2022 prefixes and was the source of the outdated note; suggested citing the current BIPM brochure for interpretive notes. | SP 811 is kept as the public-domain content source for unit names, symbols and quantities, which all match the current brochure. Its one interpretive note is no longer used: the angle notes follow BIPM Section 2.3.3 (method step 7). NIST SP 330 stays unused because of its BIPM copyright notice (round 0). | fixed |
